summary: Official yearly figures now exist for the UK and Ontario: HMRC's own annual reports print total informant payments for 2018/19-2020/21 and 2023/24-2025/26 (record £1.388m in 2025/26, including the first months of the Strengthened Reward Scheme), and the OSC's audited statements give payments to whistleblowers every fiscal year 2018/19-2025/26 (nil in 2025/26). The Strengthened Reward Scheme took effect on 26 Nov 2025, not 6 Apr 2026; no SRS payment is reported yet, and the SFO still has no scheme (only a feasibility commitment and the Fisher review's recommendation). In Europe, five reward schemes with official rules were added (UK CMA, Hungary GVH, Slovakia Antimonopoly Office and Ministry of Justice, Lithuania Competition Council) plus Lithuania's no-cap rule and 2023-2024 Prosecutor figures; payment data outside the UK and Ontario remain scarce.

Az informátori díj összege az eljáró versenytanács által az ügyben kiszabott bírság egy százaléka, de legfeljebb ötvenmillió forint.

Odmena za poskytnutie dôkazov o karteli predstavuje 1 % z uložených pokút v jednom rozhodnutí úradu, maximálne 100 000 EUR.

cases.summary: First Hungarian competition case opened largely on information from a person who applied for the informant reward: cartel on the office-supplies market, fines on eleven firms.
cases.quote: a GVH tizenegy vállalkozással szemben összesen 1.003,6 millió Ft bírságot szabott ki. [...] amely a vonatkozó ügyben meghaladta a 10 millió forintot.
cases.notes: Fine printed as 1.003,6 millió Ft. Award 'meghaladta a 10 millió forintot' (more than HUF 10 million): value is a lower bound. The 2014 report lists a press conference on 24 Jan 2014 on the first cartel case with an informant reward payment.

events.title: Autumn Budget 2024 promises stronger HMRC informant rewards
events.description: The government commits to strengthening HMRC's scheme for rewarding informants about high-value tax fraud and avoidance.
events.quote: Rewards for informants – The government will strengthen HMRC’s scheme for rewarding informants, to encourage reporting of high value tax fraud and avoidance.

events.title: Treasury minister announces a percentage-based HMRC reward scheme
events.description: The Exchequer Secretary announces a new HMRC scheme for informants, inspired by US and Canadian models, paying a percentage of the tax collected, to launch later in 2025.
events.quote: I am glad to announce today that HMRC will launch a new reward scheme for informants later this year

events.title: Treasury: annual totals only, no counts or individual rewards
events.description: Answering a written question, the Treasury confirms the scheme launched on 26 Nov 2025 and says HMRC will keep publishing the annual total of rewards but not the number or size of rewards.
events.quote: To protect the confidentiality of informants we do not publish the number of rewards or size of individual rewards.

events.title: Anti-Corruption Strategy: government to assess financial incentives for reporting economic crime
events.description: The UK Anti-Corruption Strategy commits to consider the Fisher review's findings on incentivising whistleblowers and assess the feasibility of financial incentive schemes.
events.quote: assess the feasibility of introducing financial incentive schemes and support for individuals reporting economic crime

events.title: Draft law: 45% tax withheld from Strengthened Reward Scheme payments
events.description: HMRC publishes draft Finance Bill 2026-27 legislation requiring it to deduct income tax at the additional rate (45%) from rewards under the Strengthened Reward Scheme; effective from Royal Assent.
events.quote: receive this payment with Income Tax due deducted at source at the additional rate of 45%

events.title: Independent review recommends SFO whistleblower rewards
events.description: The Fisher review's second report recommends legislation letting the Serious Fraud Office financially reward whistleblowers, with a consultation on scheme design, plus offences for false reports and harassment.
events.quote: Make legislative provision for the Serious Fraud Office to financially reward whistleblowers. The Government should launch a consultation to inform the design of a suitable scheme.

events.title: CMA raises cartel informant reward cap to £250,000
events.description: The Competition and Markets Authority raises the maximum reward for information about cartels from £100,000 to £250,000.
events.quote: offering a reward of up to £250,000, increased from £100,000, to people who tell the CMA about unlawful cartel activity they have witnessed

events.title: Lithuania lets its competition authority pay whistleblowers
events.description: The Seimas adopts amendments to the Law on Competition allowing the Competition Council to pay a one-off reward of 1% of fines (EUR 1,000-100,000) for information on anti-competitive agreements.
events.quote: Konkurencijos taryba would pay whistleblowers a single payment (from EUR 1,000 to EUR 100,000) constituting 1 percent of the fines imposed on the infringers

events.title: Lithuanian Competition Council rewards take effect
events.description: Rewards for evidence of cartels and other anti-competitive agreements become available from 1 July 2019.
events.quote: From July 1 persons who provide evidence enabling Konkurencijos taryba to detect anti-competitive agreements will be entitled to a financial reward.

events.title: Slovak Antimonopoly Office introduces cartel informant reward
events.description: An amendment to the Competition Act (136/2001) introduces a reward for natural persons who provide evidence of a cartel: 1% of fines, up to EUR 100,000.
events.quote: Úplnou novinkou v slovenskej súťažnej praxi je zavedenie inštitútu oznamovateľa, t.j. finančnej odmeny pre fyzické osoby za predloženie dôkazov o karteli.

events.title: Slovak whistleblower act with Ministry of Justice rewards takes effect
events.description: Act 307/2014 takes effect: the Ministry of Justice may grant whistleblowers a reward of up to 50 times the minimum wage after a final conviction or administrative decision.

events.title: New Slovak Competition Act keeps the cartel informant reward
events.description: Act 187/2021 replaces Act 136/2001 and keeps the 1% / EUR 100,000 reward in § 53, as a legal entitlement.

events.title: Hungary introduces informant reward for cartel evidence
events.description: An amendment to the Hungarian Competition Act (Tpvt.) introduces a reward of 1% of the fine, up to HUF 50 million, for people who provide indispensable written evidence of hard-core cartels.
events.quote: 2010. április 1-jével lépett hatályba a Tpvt. azon módosítása, amely bevezette az ún. informátori díj intézményét.

events.title: GVH press conference on first cartel case with an informant reward payment
events.description: The Hungarian Competition Authority holds a press conference on the first cartel case in which an informant reward was paid (office supplies, Vj-43/2011).
events.quote: január 24. Sajtótájékoztató az első informátori díjkifizetéssel érintett kartell ügyében.

events.title: Australian parliamentary committee recommends whistleblower rewards
events.description: The Parliamentary Joint Committee on Corporations and Financial Services recommends that a whistleblower protection body or law enforcement agencies may pay rewards set as a percentage of penalties imposed.
events.quote: a whistleblower protection body (such as that recommended in Chapter 12) or prescribed law enforcement agencies may give a ‘reward’ to any relevant whistleblower.

events.title: Australian government defers a whistleblower reward scheme
events.description: The government only 'notes' the reward recommendations and says a post-implementation review will assess the merit and cost of a rewards scheme.
events.quote: This will provide the opportunity to assess the merit and cost case of a rewards scheme when the present reforms have had a reasonable time to operate and further information is available.

events.title: Treasury opens statutory review of tax and corporate whistleblowing laws
events.description: Treasury's statutory review under s 1317AK of the Corporations Act consults until 29 July 2026; press reports say the paper discusses financial incentives (paper not read).
events.quote: Help us identify issues by responding to this consultation by 29 July 2026 .

programs.name: Competition and Markets Authority rewards for information about cartels
programs.notes: The CMA (formerly the Office of Fair Trading) pays discretionary rewards to people with inside information about cartels, at the end of an investigation; the amount depends on the value of the information and the harm, not a fixed share of fines. Cap £100,000, raised to £250,000 on 6 Jun 2023. Rests on internal policy, not statute (Fisher review). Launch (OFT, reportedly Feb 2008) not confirmed in an official document read; no figures on rewards paid published.

programs.name: Hungarian Competition Authority informant reward (informátori díj, Tpvt. § 79/A)
programs.notes: A natural person who gives the GVH indispensable written evidence (or information enabling a dawn raid) of a hard-core cartel gets 1% of the total fine, up to HUF 50 million, tax-free, once the competition council fines the firms. About 20 inquiries a year in 2010-2016; first reward paid in the office-supplies case (Vj-43/2011, fine HUF 1,003.6 million, reward above HUF 10 million). No yearly payment totals published.

programs.name: Slovak Antimonopoly Office reward for cartel evidence (§ 53 Act 187/2021; formerly Act 136/2001)
programs.notes: The first natural person to give the Antimonopoly Office decisive evidence of a cartel is entitled to 1% of the fines on all parties, up to EUR 100,000, once the decision is final and fines paid (50%, max EUR 10,000, if fines go unpaid). Introduced 1 Jul 2014; kept in the 2021 Competition Act. Annual reports 2014-2024 report no reward paid.

programs.name: Slovak Ministry of Justice whistleblower rewards (Act 307/2014, § 9)
programs.notes: Predecessor of the Whistleblower Protection Office rewards (svk-uoo-rewards): the Ministry of Justice could grant up to 50 times the minimum wage after a final conviction or administrative decision, on request within six months; no legal entitlement and no court review. Replaced by Act 54/2019; exact end date and any figures on rewards paid not found.

programs.name: Lithuanian Competition Council whistleblower remuneration (Law on Competition)
programs.notes: One-off reward for evidence of cartels and other anti-competitive agreements: 1% of the fines imposed, between EUR 1,000 and EUR 100,000; amount weighs the evidence's added value, severity and the informant's risk. Still advertised in May 2026. No figures on rewards paid found.

new_indicators.name: Forecast Exchequer yield of a reward measure
new_indicators.definition: Official forecast of the extra net tax revenue a reward measure is expected to bring in a future year (e.g. a costing certified by a fiscal council). Always status projection.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed for the UK Budget 2025 costing of the Strengthened Reward Scheme.

new_indicators.name: Award applications admitted
new_indicators.definition: Reward applications an authority formally admitted for consideration (e.g. Hungarian GVH 'befogadott kérelem'), as opposed to all inquiries or applications received.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed for the Hungarian GVH informant reward; could instead be a breakdown of award_applications_received.

proposed_corrections.value: Announced at Autumn Budget 2024 (30 Oct 2024) and in a Treasury speech (11 Mar 2025); launched at Budget 2025 on 26 Nov 2025 with immediate effect. 15-30% of tax collected (excluding penalties and interest) when information leads to collection of at least £1.5 million; discretionary; anonymous reports are not paid. HMRC publishes only an annual total of all informant payments (£1.388 million in 2025-26, not split by scheme). Draft Finance Bill 2026-27 legislation (Jul 2026) would withhold 45% income tax from SRS rewards. OBR-certified costing forecasts extra yield of £10m in 2027-28 rising to £95m in 2029-30. No SRS payment reported yet.
proposed_corrections.reason: The '6 April 2026' start date from advocacy sources is wrong: Budget 2025 para 5.9 ('Changes apply with immediate effect'), the policy costings ('effective from 26 November 2025') and written answer 93208 all give 26 Nov 2025.

proposed_corrections.value: HM Revenue & Customs makes discretionary payments to informants under section 26 of the Commissioners for Revenue and Customs Act 2005; the amount reflects tax recovered, revenue loss prevented and time saved, not a fixed share. HMRC's annual reports print the yearly total for 2018/19-2020/21 and 2023/24-2025/26 (£290,250 in 2018/19 to £1.388 million in 2025/26); other years come from FOI requests reported in the press or relayed by the Fisher review. HMRC does not publish the number or size of individual rewards. Complemented for large cases by the Strengthened Reward Scheme (gbr-hmrc-srs) from 26 Nov 2025.
proposed_corrections.reason: Official yearly totals found in HMRC annual reports.

proposed_corrections.value: Under the Law on the Protection of Whistleblowers (XIII-804, in force 1 Jan 2019, Art. 12) the Prosecutor General's Office may pay a one-off reward for valuable information. The law sets no maximum and no percentage: the reward is to be proportional to the damage caused or that could have been caused, and not tied to a court judgment; a commission of the Prosecutor General's Office sets the amount (Government Resolution 1133 of 14 Nov 2018). Requests and grants: 2019-2022 11 requests, 4 granted, EUR 34,000 (TI Lithuania); 2023: 3 requests, none granted; 2024: 3 requests, none granted (Prosecutor's Office activity reports).
proposed_corrections.reason: Rate and cap read in the law text; 2023-2024 figures from official reports.

proposed_corrections.value: Ontario's securities regulator pays 5-15% of monetary sanctions and voluntary payments of at least CAD 1 million, up to CAD 5 million; up to CAD 1.5 million is paid even if the OSC does not collect. Awards are discretionary; anonymous filing through a lawyer. The OSC announces individual awards by news release; its audited financial statements show payments to whistleblowers each fiscal year (to 31 March): CAD 7.5 million in 2018/19, then between nil and CAD 1.8 million a year; nil in 2025/26. No award news release between Oct 2024 and Oct 2026.
proposed_corrections.reason: Yearly payment series found in OSC financial statements.

proposed_corrections.value: The Whistleblower Protection Office (Úrad na ochranu oznamovateľov) may grant a reward of up to 50 times the minimum wage for a qualified report once an indictment is filed or an administrative offence is finally decided; the reward is not a legal entitlement and depends on merit, lost earnings and assets protected or recovered. Fixed cap, not a share of money recovered. Annual reports 2021-2025 show 7 requests in total and no reward granted (2 still pending at end-2025). From 2015 the Ministry of Justice handled rewards under Act 307/2014 (svk-msr-rewards). launched = Office's first reward requests (Sept 2021).
proposed_corrections.reason: Link to the predecessor programme now recorded.

gaps: UK HMRC: still no official total for 2021/22 and 2022/23 (the annual reports for those years do not print it; 2022/23 £508,500 only via the Fisher review citing a law-firm bulletin) nor for 2008/09-2017/18 except press reports. The original FOI response letters were not obtained: WhatDoTheyKnow sits behind a Cloudflare check (not bypassed); no HMRC FOI release on informant payments exists on gov.uk.
UK HMRC: 2023/24 total disagrees: £989,256 in the HMRC annual report vs £978,256 in the Price Bailey FOI (MoneyWeek/WNN) and the Fisher review; not resolved.
UK HMRC: the number of rewards paid per year is never published (WQ 93208: HMRC does not publish the number or size of rewards).

UK Strengthened Reward Scheme: no SRS payment, case or claim count published as of Oct 2026; the 2025-26 total (£1.388m) is not split by scheme. The '6 April 2026' start date is not supported: official documents give 26 Nov 2025.

UK SFO: no decision yet. Government committed (Anti-Corruption Strategy, Dec 2025) only to assess feasibility; the Fisher review's Recommendation 15 (Jul 2026) awaits a government response (not found).

UK FCA/PRA: no new official FCA or PRA statement on paying whistleblowers found after the 2014 note; the Fisher review relays that FCA chief executive Nikhil Rathi said in 2024 he was not opposed to remunerating individuals (second-hand, not recorded as an event).
UK CMA: start date of informant rewards (OFT, reportedly Feb 2008) not confirmed in an official document (OFT press release in the National Archives web archive not located); no data on rewards paid.

Canada OSC: no award news release found from Oct 2024 to Oct 2026 (news listing paged back to Sept 2024); FY2025/26 payments nil. No yearly tip counts published (2022 annual report gives only '+14%').
Canada CRA OTIP: no new official figures found; canada.ca still refuses scripted connections. Latest figures remain the 2019 ATIP and a 2020 CRA talk relayed by media/law firms.

Lithuania Prosecutor rewards: 2025 activity report not available (prokuraturos.lt blocks scripts; not in the Wayback Machine). Amounts paid per year after 2022 are not stated beyond 'none granted' in 2023-2024.

Lithuania Competition Council, Slovakia Antimonopoly Office, Hungary GVH: no figures on rewards actually paid (counts or amounts), apart from Hungary's first case (reward above HUF 10 million). GVH reports 2017-2025 give no informant counts.
Slovakia Ministry of Justice rewards under Act 307/2014 (2015-2019): no figures on requests or rewards found; end date (Act 54/2019 transition) not confirmed.

Poland: no reward scheme found (the 2024 whistleblower law is protection only; a KAS search turned up only staff bonuses). No other EU member state with a paying tax-informant scheme found within budget.
Australia: the 2017 committee report itself (aph.gov.au) returned 403; the 2026 Treasury consultation paper loads by script and was not read, so whether it proposes rewards is unverified.
